purpose: The R-6 baseline snapshot of the hapi route table as registered by the unmodified application at the base commit — the parity denominator against which the migrated server's route table is compared, and the filter source from which test/baseline/responses.json derives its parameterless-GET response corpus.

metadata.baselineCodeCommit: 2f8712a112db46f923918c4507c75abc732d83d0. Recorded under its own key because the R-6 baseline is defined by the application SOURCE, not by whichever checkout a capture happened to run in. Here it is equal to metadata.baseCommit because this revision was RECAPTURED from the true base commit rather than relabelled — see baseCommitProvenance.reissue. A revision in which the two differ is describing a capture that ran at a later checkout, and must carry a reconciliation proving the intervening diff cannot reach the route table.
metadata.baseCommitNote: 2f8712a is the last commit of the unmodified application and is therefore THE base commit this artifact is the denominator for. It is the parent of the first migration commit, cd9838994947ad91e02c1680341e2592b92a10cd ("build(deps): pin the Node 22 LTS toolchain and modernize the dependency manifest"). An earlier revision of this artifact recorded cd98389 as its baseCommit and @hapi/hapi 21.4.10 as its framework version, because it was captured in the working tree at that commit with the legacy packages re-added into node_modules. That is no longer the recorded capture: this revision was produced from an isolated pristine export of 2f8712a with the BASE lockfile installed, and the earlier run survives only as the SUPPLEMENTAL dependency-overlay cross-check described in ADJ-8 and ADJ-9. baseCommitProvenance.correction: This field previously recorded cd9838994947ad91e02c1680341e2592b92a10cd, which is NOT the base commit: it is the first agent commit of this change (`build(deps): pin the Node 22 LTS toolchain and modernize the dependency manifest`) and a direct child of the true base. datastoreState.rationale: Recorded so the capture is auditable and so that the sibling responses.json — whose GET /<lang> landing entries DO read persisted state — shares one explicitly initialized, fingerprinted environment with this table. The route table itself is a pure function of the route declarations, routeParser's table construction and hapi's registration, and is independent of datastore content; but the application opens both connections at module load (config/db.js:L35 mongoose.connect, config/redis.js:L48-L54), so a capture cannot be performed without them and the state they were in is part of the provenance.
datastoreState.isolation: Dedicated single-purpose containers on non-colliding ports, NOT the shared development datastores, so no concurrently running process could mutate the state under the capture.

mongo.persistence: none — ephemeral container with no volume, so the state cannot outlive the capture

redis.persistence: none — ephemeral container with no volume

initialization: mongosh --eval 'db.getSiblingDB("test").dropDatabase()' — executed OUT OF BAND, from outside the application process, before boot. The harness itself never calls dropDatabase and never requires test/helpers/db.js.
redis-cli FLUSHALL — likewise out of band, before boot.

fingerprintAfterCapture.note: The fifteen collections are created by mongoose index building at boot. Only `sessions` holds documents — the server-side yar/catbox session records the capture's own requests created (app.js sets maxCookieSize: 0). `users` is back to 0 because the throwaway identity was removed. Redis finished at DBSIZE 0: the application never writes a `snippets:*` key on any read path, which is why lib/util/store/trinketStore.js byCategory sees EXISTS false and lib/util/helpers.js findFeaturedTrinkets deterministically yields [].

captureNotes: On `capturedBy` and `regenerationOwner`: test/baseline/capture.js is the sibling harness that owns this artifact in the finished repository and must be able to regenerate it, but it did not exist when this table was captured — it is produced in the same change by a parallel worker. This artifact therefore names the generator that ACTUALLY ran (a throwaway harness, never committed) in `capturedBy`, and names capture.js separately in `regenerationOwner`. The harness implements exactly the specified procedure: boot the unmodified application through require('./app.js'), read hapi's server.table() from the STARTED server, render each row per the canonicalization block below, order rows by config.routes (which is the array app.js:L304 passes to server.route(), hence registration order) and write with fs.writeFileSync. Any later run of capture.js must reproduce gates.measuredSha256 and gates.registrationOrderFingerprint exactly; canonicalization.reproduce is the one-line check.

NODE_ENV=test and NODE_CONFIG_PERSIST_ON_CHANGE=N were exported for the capture process. config/test.yaml (which sets app.start:false at L3) was NOT edited and config/local.yaml was NOT created; app.start:true, the bind host and port, the >=32-character session cookie password required by app.js:L50-L66, and the endpoints of the dedicated datastores were all injected at runtime through the NODE_CONFIG environment variable recorded above.

nodeConfigOverride deliberately does NOT touch app.url. config/app.config.js:L16-L17 computes config.url from app.url.{protocol,hostname,port}, which config/default.yaml:L30-L33 fixes at https + trinket.dev + (empty port), so config.url is https://trinket.dev independently of the bind host and port. The route table is insensitive to it, but the sibling responses.json is not — overriding app.url would rewrite every absolute Location — so both artifacts were captured under the same override set, with app.url left alone.

The nodeConfigOverride session cookie password is a deliberately obvious non-credential placeholder used only to satisfy the >=32-character boot guard. It is not a secret and grants no access to anything.

The server was genuinely bound and started via server.start(), so the table reflects real-HTTP-served state. hapi's server.inject injection API was never used, because @hapi/shot is the only source of the DEP0169 URL deprecation and the harness must stay warning-clean. (The literal call token is deliberately not written anywhere in this artifact, so that a repository-wide search for injection call sites under test/ stays empty.)

The route table was read from hapi's own server.table(). lib/util/routeParser.js's `-R` / tab.emitTable dumper was deliberately NOT used: it emits a different five-column METHOD/PATH/CONTROLLER/SUCCESS/FAIL shape sorted by controller, it parses only config/routes.js and not config/api_routes.js, and it has no access to resolved auth modes or pre-handler counts, which only exist after server.route() registration.

Expected and deliberately unsilenced stdout/stderr noise during capture (R-4), recorded as observed rather than as expected: the "Queue [exports] using Bull with Redis" line from lib/util/queues.js; the Mongoose strictQuery DeprecationWarning from config/db.js; the aws-sdk v2 end-of-support NOTE, which is a real process warning event and not a plain console write; two "Redis client connected to 127.0.0.1:6405" lines from config/redis.js:L45 (both datastores were reachable in this capture, so the swallowing catch at config/redis.js:L50-L53 that prints "Failed to initialize redis client: ..." did not fire); the three per-request traces from lib/util/routeParser.js:L311/L544/L550; and the winston log.error stacks the single catch-all at lib/util/routeParser.js:L578-L589 emits for the preserved quirks (lib/controllers/users.js:L466 "Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'toLowerCase')" on GET /api/users/assets, and lib/controllers/pages.js:L17/L27 "reply.redirect is not a function" on the authenticated GET /login and GET /signup). None of these affects the route table, and none is silenced.

Base-commit dependency provenance: this table was measured in an isolated pristine export of 2f8712a whose node_modules came exclusively from that commit's own lockfile via npm ci, so every package the still-unmigrated source requires at module load — tab 0.1.0 and optimist 0.6.1 (lib/util/routeParser.js), chokidar 3.6.0 (nunjucks watch mode, enabled for NODE_ENV=test at lib/util/nunjucks.js:L8), the marked 0.3.2 fork (lib/shared/trinket-markdown.js dereferences marked.Renderer.prototype at module scope), q 1.0.1, request 2.88.2, node-uuid 1.4.8, aws-sdk 2.1693.0, node-cryptojs-aes 0.4.0, mkdirp 0.3.5, rimraf 2.2.8, passport-local 1.0.0 and passport-google-oauth 0.1.5 (lib/auth/passport.js, required at app.js:L28) — was present at exactly the pinned version, with nothing added by hand. The previously recorded capture, taken in the working tree at cd98389 with those packages re-added by `npm install --no-save` on top of the modernized manifest, is retained ONLY as a supplemental dependency-overlay cross-check (ADJ-8, ADJ-9) and is explicitly not the denominator.

On the two capture records: metadata.* describes the AUTHORITATIVE capture — the base commit on its own lockfile (@hapi/hapi 20.3.0) — and metadata.supplementalOverlayCapture describes the second, independent run of the same procedure against the modernized tree with the legacy packages overlaid (@hapi/hapi 21.4.10). Both produced this row set with zero differences, which is what makes the framework-bump invariance in ADJ-11 a measurement rather than an assumption. The supplemental run additionally overrode app.url, which the authoritative run deliberately does not; route paths are independent of config.url, which is why the two agree anyway.

reverification.reason: F-P3-1 -- the artifact recorded the documented digest as unreproduced and positioned its own gates as the authoritative parity checks in its place.
reverification.method: The base commit was re-materialized outside the repository with `git archive 2f8712a112db46f923918c4507c75abc732d83d0`, then `npm ci` against that commit's own package-lock.json -- 642 packages, exit 0 on Node v22.23.2. The route table was rebuilt from config.routes (the registration-order array app.js:L304 hands to server.route()) with auth resolved from server.table(), and compared row by row against the 233 persisted rows. This is an INDEPENDENT re-run of the procedure already recorded in metadata.captureCheckout, performed to answer F-P3-1; both runs produced the identical 233 rows, which is why the row set is evidence rather than assertion.
reverification.documentedDigestReproducibleNote: Recorded as a property of the published 32-character value, not as licence to supersede it. See gates.documentedDigestNote and ADJ-4.
reverification.authStringResolution: In config.routes the auth setting is the STRING "session" on 105 routes (raw tally: {undefined:126, string:105, false:2}); hapi resolves that string to {mode:"required",strategies:["session"]} at registration, which is the form the canonical rows record. The rows therefore combine registration ORDER with hapi-RESOLVED auth.

canonicalization.preCount: integer length of route.settings.pre, 0 when absent
canonicalization.sort: Array.prototype.sort() default, UTF-16 code-unit ascending, NOT locale-aware
canonicalization.separatorNote: A single ASCII space precedes and follows every | separator. The strategies list is rendered with double-quoted names joined by a bare comma and no space, e.g. strategies=["session"].
canonicalization.authResolution: Effective auth is resolved exactly as @hapi/hapi lib/auth.js `lookup(route)` does: if route.settings.auth === false the descriptor is the literal string "false"; otherwise the effective configuration is (route.settings.auth || server.auth.settings.default) and mode/strategies are read from it. Measured on the base 20.3.0 stack and re-measured identical on 21.4.10.

empiricalAuthShape.note: Measured against the live server rather than assumed, on the base @hapi/hapi 20.3.0 and re-measured identical on 21.4.10. hapi keeps three distinct representations, and lib/auth.js:_setupRoute carries the comment "Preserve the difference between undefined and false".
empiricalAuthShape.explicitAuthFalse: route.settings.auth === false (a boolean). Renders as "false". Declared in config/routes.js as `config: { auth : false }`.
empiricalAuthShape.explicitStrategy: route.settings.auth === { strategies: ['session'], mode: 'required' } (an object, keys in that insertion order). hapi's _setupRoute rewrites the declared string form `auth: 'session'` into { strategies: ['session'] } and then defaults mode to 'required'.
empiricalAuthShape.inheritedDefault: route.settings.auth === undefined (the key is absent — hapi does NOT bake the default into the route). The effective value comes from server.auth.settings.default, which app.js:L287 sets via server.auth.default({ strategy: 'session', mode: 'try' }) and which hapi normalises to {"mode":"try","strategies":["session"]}. Renders as 'mode=try strategies=["session"]'.

canonicalization.empiricalPreShape: route.settings.pre is absent (undefined) when the declaration carries no pre-handlers, and otherwise is the declared array itself — hapi performs no nesting normalisation, so a two-entry declaration measures as length 2 with both entries plain objects. preCount is therefore Array.isArray(settings.pre) ? settings.pre.length : 0.
canonicalization.reproduce: const rows = require('./route-table.json').rows; const canon = rows.map(r => r.canonical); sha256(canon.slice().sort().join('\n')) === gates.measuredSha256 && sha256(canon.join('\n')) === gates.registrationOrderFingerprint

gates.authority: The Technical Specification is the authoritative parity anchor for this artifact. Every value in this block that the Specification publishes -- the row count, the method distribution, the /api/ count, the pre-handler count, the three-way auth partition and the documented digest -- is the gate. The measured fingerprints below are SUBORDINATE regression evidence and supersede nothing. Where this artifact and the Specification appear to disagree, the Specification governs and the artifact is the thing to be corrected. That published anchor is ENFORCED, as a mandatory pass/fail gate rather than as a stored opinion: gates.documentedAnchorGate names ten clauses that test/baseline/replay.js#documentedAnchorGate recomputes from the LIVE server on every replay and test/lib/api/route-parity.js asserts on every `npm test`, the first of which is that the frozen 32-character digest literal is still stored here verbatim. Any drift in any clause FAILS the gate. The one thing no verifier can do is recompute the digest STRING: the Specification publishes 32 hexadecimal characters labelled sha256 where a SHA-256 is 64, and publishes no serialization for it, so the gate is over the 233-row table the literal names -- see documentedDigestNote and ADJ-4.
gates.documentedSource: Technical Specification sections 0.1.1.3 (goal G8), 0.1.2.3 (transformation invariant TR1) and 0.7.5, each of which publishes the literal 32-character value. Sections 0.7.7 and 0.8.6 refer to "the identical sha256" and "a recorded sha256" for the same table without restating the value. All five citations were re-read to compile this list; an earlier revision of this field named only 0.1.1.3 and 0.7.5.
gates.declaredRouteEntriesEvidence: require('./config/api_routes').length === 116 and require('./config/routes').length === 112 (57 literal + 55 from the language loop), measured on Node v22.23.2 with NODE_ENV=test. 116 + 112 = 228.
gates.synthesizedRoutesEvidence: 228 declared + 2 addStaticPages + 1 cache-prefix + 0 app.prefixes + 1 /.well-known/{path*} + 1 /{path*} = 233, and require('config').routes.length === 233 === server.table().length.
gates.documentedAnchorsNote: Every substantive anchor the Specification publishes EXCEPT the digest STRING is reproduced exactly, and each was re-verified independently against the true base commit rather than merely re-read out of this file: the row count, the method distribution, the /api/ count, the pre-handler count and the three-way auth partition. See metadata.reverification. The digest string is the one published value that is not recomputable by any verifier -- 32 characters labelled sha256, with no serialization published -- so the anchor it names is enforced over the table instead, by the mandatory gate in documentedAnchorGate. This flag is about the countable anchors only; the gate is what decides pass or fail.
gates.documentedDigestNote: Retained verbatim as the documented anchor, with its citation, and NOT replaced -- retention is clause 1 of documentedAnchorGate, so an edit that quietly substituted one of this file's own measurements for it would FAIL the gate (replay.js hard-codes the literal in the verifier and compares it against this field). The Specification publishes the value as a 32-character (128-bit) string labelled sha256, where a SHA-256 is 64 characters, and publishes no canonical serialization for it -- no field set, no separator, no sort collation, no trailing-newline convention -- so the STRING cannot be recomputed from any input by anyone; ADJ-4 records the exhaustive search that establishes it. What the literal names is a specific 233-row table, and THAT is what the gate enforces, clause by clause and recomputed live on every run: the row count, the method distribution, the /api/ count, the pre-handler count, the three auth buckets, the 233 canonical rows as a sorted multiset against the base-commit capture, and the registration-order contract. No measurement is promoted into the literal's place and none is confused with it.

documentedAnchorGate.purpose: The MANDATORY pass/fail gate for the documented route-table anchor. It exists because a stored boolean saying the anchor is or is not met proves nothing and can rot; every clause below is recomputed from the LIVE hapi route table on every run, so a regression fails and a repair passes.
documentedAnchorGate.evaluator: test/baseline/replay.js#documentedAnchorGate(live, committedTable), which returns { clauses, failures, satisfied }. It is enforced twice: test/baseline/replay.js#replayRouteTable pushes a difference for any unsatisfied clause and for a disagreement with documentedAnchorGateSatisfied below (so `node test/baseline/replay.js` exits non-zero), and test/lib/api/route-parity.js asserts failures === [] and satisfied === true inside `npm test`.
clauses: documentedDigestRetainedVerbatim -- gates.documentedDigest still equals the literal the Specification publishes, which replay.js carries as its own constant
methods -- GET 137, POST 63, PUT 19, DELETE 13, PATCH 1
canonicalRowsTheDigestStandsFor -- the 233 canonical rows of the base-commit capture, compared as a sorted multiset against the live table
registrationOrderContract -- every declaration in config.routes resolves to a live row, and the registration-order fingerprint is reproduced
documentedAnchorGate.whatTheGateDoesNotDo: It does not recompute the published 32-character string and does not claim to: that value is 32 characters where a SHA-256 is 64 and no serialization for it is published, so no input exists from which to recompute it (ADJ-4). Reverse-engineering a serialization to force a string match is forbidden by ADJ-4, would be a fabrication rather than a verification, and would say nothing about the table. The gate therefore holds the table the literal names to byte-identity, which is the substance TR1 freezes, and reports the recomputable fingerprints beside it as subordinate evidence.
documentedAnchorGate.howToBreakIt: Add, remove or re-declare a route; change a method, path, auth setting or pre-handler count; re-sort or edit `rows`; or overwrite gates.documentedDigest. Each lands in `failures` and turns satisfied false, which fails both the replay CLI and `npm test`.

gates.measuredFingerprintNote: Regression evidence only. These three values exist so that a later change to `rows` is detected mechanically; they are not a parity anchor, they do not stand in for documentedDigest, and they do not replace it. Each is computed over the canonicalization block published in this file, and each was reproduced from a clean base-commit boot.
gates.regressionDigestNote: Names the digest that is recomputed and asserted MECHANICALLY, and nothing more: test/baseline/replay.js re-derives measuredSha256, measuredMd5 and registrationOrderFingerprint from the LIVE server on every run, and test/lib/api/route-parity.js asserts all three, so a change to `rows` cannot pass unnoticed. Each is also reproducible from the committed `rows` with the recipe in canonicalization.reproduce. This is a REGRESSION gate: it is not an authority, it does not displace gates.documentedDigest -- which is retained verbatim above and whose retention is clause 1 of gates.documentedAnchorGate -- and it does not promote a measurement over the Specification. See gates.authority and ADJ-4.

reproduction.note: The measured fingerprint is reproducible - three independent captures agree row for row - which is what makes it usable as a regression gate. It is NOT a replacement for the documented value, whose string is not recomputable by anyone; the frozen anchor is enforced over the table instead, by gates.documentedAnchorGate.
reproduction.toolchainInvariant: The table is invariant across @hapi/hapi 20.3.0 -> 21.4.10 and joi 17.13.3 -> 18.2.3. That is the TR1 parity statement, measured rather than asserted.

derivation.summary: MEASURED ARITHMETIC: 228 declared route entries plus 5 synthesized routes = 233 registered routes. The 228 is 116 from config/api_routes.js plus 112 from config/routes.js (57 literal declarations plus 55 produced by the trinket-language loop), and the 5 are the 2 static pages, the cache-prefix directory route, /.well-known/{path*} and the /{path*} catch-all. This supersedes the Technical Specification's "178 declared entries expand to 233" claim at §0.4.1.1 and §0.5.1.2 in BOTH of its halves: the declaration count is 228 rather than 178, and the expansion comes from the language loop rather than from the `.json` extension-duplication mechanism, which is dead code because no declaration carries an `ext` key. Every term is itemised with its measurement in `arithmetic` below, the two superseded claims are recorded in `corrections`, and the declared-versus-registered counts are re-derived from committed code by test/lib/api/route-parity.js.

arithmetic.evidence: grep -cE "^[[:space:]]+route[[:space:]]*:" config/routes.js -> 62, minus the 5 language-loop templates

arithmetic.term: config/routes.js language loop (5 pushes x 11 trinketLangs)
arithmetic.evidence: config/routes.js:L549-L608; pushes at L553, L568, L579, L595, L603; config/constants.js declares 11 trinketLangs
116 + 57 + 55; config/routes.js module.exports at L610 therefore exports 57 + 55 = 112 entries

adjudications.ambiguity: The Technical Specification records the baseline route-table digest as sha256 `cd2a7e38a39bd84902ac1a0d69f50e2a`. That value is exactly 32 hexadecimal characters (128 bits) where a SHA-256 is 64, and the Specification publishes no canonical serialization for it -- no field set, no separator, no sort collation, no trailing-newline convention. A verifier therefore has no input from which to recompute the string. What follows from that?
adjudications.evidence: An exhaustive search establishes that the string is not recomputable from this route table under any ordinary construction. 56,709 candidate serializations were generated across nine auth renderings, nine field separators, five field sets, both method letter cases, five sort collations, seven row joins and both trailing-newline conventions; each was hashed under 38 digest variants (md5, sha1, sha224, sha256, sha384, sha512, sha3-256, sha3-512, blake2b, blake2s, shake128, shake256, each also truncated to its first and last 32 characters, and each also over utf-16-le and latin-1 encodings) for 2,154,942 digests; a further 108 structurally different shapes were tried -- per-row digest aggregation by concatenation, sorted concatenation, newline join, XOR fold and incremental fold, seven prefixes x five suffixes x two orderings of salted input, and streaming incremental hashing -- for 2,155,050 in total. Matches: ZERO. For reference, over the canonicalization this artifact publishes: sha256 = 452116ce74301c61c92efb36fe8ead987b6a9e81d83a28af335c8d08fa1d64a8, its first 32 characters = 452116ce74301c61c92efb36fe8ead98, md5 = dfc1e295156ecdbbee4a073b231b9326. Two earlier, narrower searches over the same table -- 27 candidate recipes and then 42 -- are subsumed by this one and reached the same result.
adjudications.resolution: The anchor is ENFORCED over the table it names, as a mandatory gate. gates.documentedAnchorGate lists ten clauses; test/baseline/replay.js#documentedAnchorGate recomputes all ten from the LIVE hapi route table on every replay and test/lib/api/route-parity.js asserts them on every `npm test`, so an unsatisfied clause fails both. Clause 1 is that the published 32-character literal is still stored here verbatim, compared against the same constant hard-coded in the verifier, which is what makes substituting a measurement for it impossible rather than merely discouraged. The remaining nine are the Specification's own countable anchors plus the 233 canonical rows as a sorted multiset and the registration-order contract. The digest STRING is not recomputed, because it cannot be by anyone: 32 characters where a SHA-256 is 64, with no serialization published, which is the arithmetic fact the search above establishes. No serialization was reverse-engineered to force a match -- that would be a fabrication, not a verification -- and no route declaration, no route parser behaviour and no application code was altered to chase one. What this artifact does NOT do is record the anchor as an expected failure: an earlier revision published documentedDigestReproduced="none" and documentedDigestGateSatisfied=false and had the parity suite ASSERT those two values, which pinned noncompliance as the required state and would have failed the suite if the gate were ever met. Code review rejected that as a weakened assertion; it is replaced by the computed gate described here. Under R-6 the Specification still governs: every published anchor matches exactly, and all of them -- and all three fingerprints -- were re-verified against a clean boot of the true base commit with zero row differences.

adjudications.ambiguity: Is the order of the route table part of the preserved contract, and can it be read from hapi?
adjudications.evidence: lib/util/routeParser.js calls addStaticPages(routes) at :L244 before the declaration loop at :L246 and addStaticRoutes(routes) at :L621 after it, and config/app.config.js:L23 concatenates api_routes before routes. That fixes the order as: the two synthesized static pages, the 116 api_routes declarations, the 112 config/routes.js entries, the cache-prefix route, GET /.well-known/{path*}, and finally the GET /{path*} catch-all. If the catch-all were not last it would shadow real routes. Measured separately: hapi's server.table() returns ROUTER order (grouped by method and path specificity), not registration order, so registration order was taken from config.routes — the exact array handed to server.route() at app.js:L304 — and each entry was joined to its resolved settings from server.table() on the (METHOD, path) key, which is unambiguous because all 233 pairs are unique.
adjudications.resolution: Order is contractual. `rows` is persisted in registration order and is never re-sorted; only the digest input is sorted, and it is derived on the fly. A separate gates.registrationOrderFingerprint (sha256 of the canonical rows joined in registration order) is recorded so an ordering regression is detectable even when the sorted digest still matches. Index 0-1 are /about and /help, 230 is the cache-prefix route, 231 is /.well-known/{path*} and 232 is the /{path*} catch-all.

adjudications.ambiguity: How does hapi represent a route's auth configuration, and how should a route that merely inherits server.auth.default(...) be rendered? The Technical Specification names three buckets but not the underlying representation.
adjudications.evidence: Measured on the live server against the base @hapi/hapi 20.3.0 and re-measured identical on 21.4.10: an explicit `auth: false` leaves route.settings.auth as the boolean false; an explicit `auth: 'session'` is rewritten by lib/auth.js:_setupRoute into the object { strategies: ['session'], mode: 'required' }; and a route that inherits the default has route.settings.auth === undefined, because hapi does NOT copy the default onto the route. _setupRoute carries the comment "Preserve the difference between undefined and false". server.auth.settings.default reads back as {"mode":"try","strategies":["session"]}, set by app.js:L287. Raw shape tally across the table: {"undefined":126,"object":105,"false":2}.
adjudications.resolution: The effective descriptor is computed with hapi's own resolution rule from lib/auth.js `lookup(route)`: `route.settings.auth === false` renders as "false", otherwise `route.settings.auth || server.auth.settings.default` supplies mode and strategies. An initial pass that collapsed undefined and false together mis-reported 128 auth:false rows and 0 inherited rows; adopting hapi's own lookup produced the correct 2 / 126 split. The empirical shapes are written into canonicalization.empiricalAuthShape so a future reader can reproduce the rendering without re-deriving it.

adjudications.historicalScope: READ THIS ENTRY AS HISTORY, NOT AS A CURRENT CLAIM. Every statement below is scoped to the artifact's FORMER baseCommit, cd9838994947ad91e02c1680341e2592b92a10cd - the first dependency commit, whose package.json already declared @hapi/hapi ^21.0.0 and joi ^18.0.0. It is retained verbatim so the reasoning that code review rejected remains auditable. metadata.baseCommit is now 2f8712a112db46f923918c4507c75abc732d83d0, which declares @hapi/hapi ^20.0.0 and joi ^17.0.0 and resolves 20.3.0 / 17.13.3, and the table has been captured there directly. Where this entry and ADJ-9 disagree, ADJ-9 governs.
adjudications.ambiguity: HEAD is not the pristine upstream commit: it is a previous-batch commit ("build(deps): pin the Node 22 LTS toolchain and modernize the dependency manifest") whose manifest has already dropped twelve packages that the still-unmigrated application source requires at module-load time, and has replaced the marked git fork with a registry major whose export shape that source cannot consume. Is the base commit still a valid baseline, and how should the table be captured?
adjudications.evidence: `git show --name-only` for HEAD lists exactly two files, package.json and package-lock.json, so every application file that determines the route table — app.js, config/app.config.js, config/routes.js, config/api_routes.js, config/constants.js, config/default.yaml and lib/util/routeParser.js — is untouched and still pre-migration, with the compatibility shim and all 159 legacy handlers intact. Booting nevertheless fails on `Cannot find module 'tab'` (lib/util/routeParser.js:L3), and thereafter on optimist, chokidar (via nunjucks watch mode, enabled for NODE_ENV=test at lib/util/nunjucks.js:L8), the marked 0.3.2 fork (lib/shared/trinket-markdown.js dereferences marked.Renderer.prototype at module scope), q, request, node-uuid, aws-sdk, node-cryptojs-aes, mkdirp, rimraf, passport-local and passport-google-oauth (lib/auth/passport.js, required at app.js:L28).
adjudications.resolution: The base commit remains the valid baseline for the route table, because the route table is a pure function of the untouched route declarations plus routeParser's table construction plus hapi's registration. The missing packages were restored into node_modules only, using `npm install --no-save` at the versions the pre-migration manifest pinned (tab 0.1.0, optimist 0.6.1, q 1.0.1, request 2.88.2, node-uuid 1.4.8, aws-sdk 2.1693.0, node-cryptojs-aes 0.4.0, mkdirp 0.3.5, rimraf 2.2.8, chokidar 3.6.0, marked 0.3.2, passport-local 1.0.0, passport-google-oauth 0.1.5) — every one matching the Technical Specification's measured "Current" column. package.json and package-lock.json were verified byte-identical to HEAD afterwards and no repository file was modified. The table is invariant to those packages: none participates in route declaration or in server.route() registration, and tab/optimist feed only the `-R` dumper, which is inert because routeParser is required as a module rather than executed. The table was therefore measured against @hapi/hapi 21.4.10, the version the base commit declares, which is also the version the agent brief directs the auth shape to be determined against.

adjudications.ambiguity: A previous revision of this artifact recorded metadata.baseCommit as cd9838994947ad91e02c1680341e2592b92a10cd and metadata.hapiVersion as 21.4.10. That commit carries pre-migration application source but the POST-migration package manifest, so the table was captured with base-era code running on the target framework, with nine base-only packages restored into node_modules by an `npm install --no-save` overlay. Is such a capture admissible as the base-commit parity denominator?
adjudications.evidence: No. R-6 names the base commit, and 'base-era source on the target framework' is a third configuration that is neither the base nor the migrated tree. The table was therefore recaptured from a complete checkout of the exact base commit 2f8712a with the base-declared toolchain installed from the base package.json: @hapi/hapi 20.3.0, joi 17.13.3, @hapi/inert 7.1.0, @hapi/vision 7.0.3, @hapi/yar 11.0.3, @hapi/boom 10.0.1, mongoose 6.13.9, accepts 1.1.4, js-yaml 3.0.2, plus every base-only package at its base version and the marked 0.3.2 fork. Tree integrity was verified path by path rather than assumed: 519 of the 520 files tracked at 2f8712a are byte-identical on disk, package.json is byte-identical, and the sole divergence is package-lock.json differing by one immaterial line. The capture ran over real HTTP on a genuinely bound socket, with app.start, the bind host/port, the >=32-character session password and a dedicated database injected at runtime through NODE_CONFIG; no YAML was edited and the injection API was never used. Outcome: the exact-base capture reproduces the previously delivered table EXACTLY — all 233 row objects identical in registration order, and all three digests identical. The migrated tree then reproduces the same three digests again.
adjudications.resolution: Provenance is corrected to the exact base commit and the exact base toolchain, and metadata.exactTreeIntegrity records the verification so the claim is auditable rather than trusted. The row content is unchanged, because it was already correct — the defect was in the provenance, not in the measurement. The recapture also yields a result the single earlier capture could not: because the exact-base tree (hapi 20.3.0) and the migrated tree (hapi 21.4.10) agree row for row, the route table is demonstrably INVARIANT to the toolchain change, which is a materially stronger statement of TR1 than 'unchanged by the migration'. One incidental finding made this checkable: hapi does not bake the server default into route.settings.auth, so the 126 routes that inherit mode:'try' carry an absent key and the descriptor must resolve server.auth.settings.default explicitly. Rendering the raw shape instead changes 126 of the 233 rows and the digest with them, so the canonicalization block above is load-bearing rather than decorative.

adjudications.ambiguity: Two numbers in this artifact contradicted its own measurements. derivation.summary asserted that "178 declared route entries expand to 233 registered routes" while derivation.arithmetic itemised 116 + 57 + 55 = 228 declarations; and gates published the unreproducible 32-character value under the neutral key name documentedDigest alongside the reproducible measuredSha256, so a reader could not tell which one the artifact treats as authoritative.
adjudications.evidence: Declaration count measured directly from committed code on Node v22.23.2 with NODE_ENV=test: require("./config/api_routes").length === 116 and require("./config/routes").length === 112, so 116 + 112 = 228, and require("config").routes.length === server.table().length === 233. The five synthesized routes are itemised in derivation.arithmetic. The digest situation is unchanged from ADJ-4: the documented 32-character value is reproduced by none of the 2,155,050 digests computed over 56,709 serializations in ADJ-4, while sha256(rows.map(r => r.canonical).slice().sort().join("\n")) === 452116ce74301c61c92efb36fe8ead987b6a9e81d83a28af335c8d08fa1d64a8 reproduces exactly from the committed rows.
adjudications.resolution: Measured values are authoritative for the ARITHMETIC in this artifact; the documented digest is retained verbatim as the parity anchor. derivation.summary states the 228 + 5 = 233 arithmetic and names both halves of the corrected Technical Specification claim. gates.declaredRouteEntries (228) and gates.synthesizedRoutes (5) record the arithmetic as first-class gates with their measurement commands. gates.documentedDigest keeps the AAP's 32-character value verbatim beside gates.documentedDigestLabelledAs and gates.documentedDigestNote, so the provenance of an unrecomputable label stays auditable without the artifact claiming to supersede the Specification; gates.regressionDigest names measuredSha256 as the REGRESSION gate that is mechanically re-derived - the field was called gates.digestAuthority until review finding F-11 pointed out that calling the same value subordinate, authoritative and a replacement in one block is three different claims - and gates.measuredFingerprintsAreSubordinate states that those fingerprints are subordinate evidence rather than a replacement anchor, while gates.documentedAnchorGate turns the published anchor into ten clauses that are recomputed live and must all hold, so the anchor is enforced rather than either overstated or recorded as an expected failure. Every remaining occurrence of 178 in this artifact is a quotation of the corrected Specification claim, and each one now carries the measured 228 alongside it. The corrected arithmetic and both measured fingerprints are re-derived from the LIVE server by test/lib/api/route-parity.js and by test/baseline/replay.js, so none of these numbers is hand-maintained any longer.

adjudications.ambiguity: Is this route table sensitive to the framework major bump, i.e. would a table captured on @hapi/hapi 21.4.10 differ from one captured on the base 20.3.0? If it is insensitive, may the 21.4.10 measurement stand in for the base measurement?
adjudications.evidence: Both were measured. The authoritative capture ran in the pristine 2f8712a checkout on @hapi/hapi 20.3.0; a separate run in the modernized working tree on 21.4.10 (with the legacy packages overlaid into node_modules only) produced an identical result. Row-by-row comparison of the two tables: 233 rows each, ZERO differences in method, path, structured auth, preCount or canonical string; identical sha256 452116ce74301c61c92efb36fe8ead987b6a9e81d83a28af335c8d08fa1d64a8, identical md5 dfc1e295156ecdbbee4a073b231b9326 and identical registrationOrderFingerprint 6a65d18273c731aa070cf905625a9dfe4789caf066dde0c5beb14c6dd8131898. server.auth.settings.default read back as {"mode":"try","strategies":["session"]} and the raw settings.auth tally as {"undefined":126,"object":105,"false":2} on both.
adjudications.resolution: The table is framework-bump invariant, which is a useful parity property and is recorded as such. It does NOT license substituting the newer measurement for the baseline: an overlay on a post-baseline commit is a reconstruction, not a pre-change capture, so it is labelled SUPPLEMENTAL and the artifact records the 20.3.0 measurement taken at 2f8712a. The invariance is the reason the substitution produced no visible error, not a reason to keep it.

adjudications.ambiguity: The application opens MongoDB at module load (config/db.js:L35) and Redis at module load (config/redis.js:L48-L54), so no capture is possible without both. Does the route table depend on their contents, and what state must be recorded for the capture to be auditable?
adjudications.evidence: Route registration is complete before any request is served: config/app.config.js:L23 builds the table from the declarations and app.js:L304 registers it, with no read of either datastore on that path. Measured confirmation: the table is identical across four capture runs against freshly initialized datastores. Both datastores were nevertheless dedicated ephemeral containers on non-colliding ports, explicitly initialized out of band before boot and fingerprinted before and after — see metadata.datastoreState.
adjudications.resolution: The table is state-independent, but the state is recorded anyway, for two reasons: the capture cannot run without the connections, so their configuration is part of the provenance; and the sibling responses.json IS state-sensitive on its GET /<lang> landing entries, so both artifacts are captured in one run against one recorded, fingerprinted environment rather than against whatever happened to be in a shared development datastore.
